Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) was rejected for every tested request, across north/south/east regions and refund, shipment, and claim types. Do not select C.
- Option B (“priority desk”) was rejected for a large north-region refund (REQ-2400). Do not infer priority routing solely from large size or repeated requests.
- No successful assignments observed yet. Given repeated rejection of C and one rejection of B, use A (“standard queue”) as the current safest default unless new evidence establishes a specific exception.
- Region, request type, size, sender department, and urgency cues have not yet demonstrated a valid alternative routing rule.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) was rejected in all earlier tested cases. No successful C assignment has been observed; continue avoiding C.
- Option B (“priority desk”) was rejected for a large north-region refund (REQ-2400). No later evidence supports using B based solely on size, urgency, repeated attempts, or other cues.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is not a safe universal default. It was accepted for four small south-region refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), across Field Sales, Regional Ops, and Client Services, including one explicitly routed through the regional office.
- Option A was rejected for: small east invoice (REQ-2410), small north claims (REQ-2415–REQ-2416), small south shipment (REQ-2417), large east invoice (REQ-2418), and small south claim (REQ-2419).
- Current strongest rule: try A for small south-region refunds. Do not generalize this success to other request types, regions, or sizes.
- For east invoices, north claims, south shipments, south claims, and large east invoices, A has demonstrated failure; B and C remain unvalidated alternatives. Avoid confidently inferring a replacement rule until an alternative succeeds.
- Sender department, urgency, size, wording (“second attempt,” scanned paperwork, or regional-office origin), and repeated requests have not independently established routing rules.

Routing notes:
- Options are A (standard queue), B (priority desk), and C (regional office). D is invalid; attempts REQ-2420–REQ-2429 using D were rejected and provide no routing evidence.
- C remains unvalidated: no successful C assignment has been observed. Continue avoiding C unless testing is necessary.
- B was rejected for a large north-region refund (REQ-2400). No evidence supports choosing B solely for size, urgency, repeated attempts, or similar cues.
- A is not a universal default. It was accepted for four small south-region refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), across multiple departments, including one regional-office-origin request.
- A was rejected for the small east invoice (REQ-2410), small north claims (REQ-2415–REQ-2416), small south shipment (REQ-2417), large east invoice (REQ-2418), and small south claim (REQ-2419).
- Strongest positive rule: try A for small south-region refunds. Do not generalize this to other request types, regions, or sizes.
- For east invoices, north claims, south shipments, south claims, and large east invoices, A has demonstrated failure; B and C remain unvalidated alternatives.
- REQ-2420–REQ-2429 add no valid assignment outcomes: all used invalid D, covering north/south/east, refunds/claims/shipments, and varied sizes or urgency cues.
- Sender department, urgency, size, wording (“second attempt,” repeated requests), and regional-office origin have not independently established routing rules. Avoid confident replacement rules until a valid alternative succeeds.

Routing notes:
- Options: A (standard queue), B (priority desk), C (regional office). D is invalid; REQ-2420–REQ-2429 using D provide no routing evidence.
- C is now validated for a large south-region claim (REQ-2442). Evidence remains limited; do not generalize beyond that case.
- A succeeded for four small south-region refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), but was rejected for east invoices, north claims, south shipments/claims, large east invoices, north large shipment (REQ-2430), north small refunds (REQ-2432, REQ-2436), east small refund (REQ-2433), and south small invoice (REQ-2449). A is not a universal default.
- B succeeded for: east small claim with urgency (REQ-2431), north small claim without urgency (REQ-2435, REQ-2448), large east invoice with urgency (REQ-2438), and large east claims (REQ-2440, REQ-2446).
- B was rejected for large north refund (REQ-2400), large south claim (REQ-2434), north small refund (REQ-2436), north small shipment (REQ-2437, REQ-2445), south small claim (REQ-2441), large east refund (REQ-2443), and north small invoice (REQ-2444). It also failed for large east invoice without the demonstrated urgency cue (REQ-2447).
- Best guidance: A for small south refunds. B has positive evidence for north small claims and east claims, especially large east claims; also for urgent large east invoices. C is a possible regional-office route for the tested large south claim.
- No reliable rule exists for most other combinations, including east/north/south refunds, shipments, and invoices. Sender department, urgency, size, repeated wording, and origin have not independently established routing rules.

Routing notes:
- Options: A (standard queue), B (priority desk), C (regional office). D is invalid; REQ-2420–REQ-2429 using D provide no routing evidence. Some tickets omit options, so an unavailable option is invalid.
- C is validated for large south claims (REQ-2442) and large south refunds (REQ-2450, REQ-2458). Evidence is still limited; repeated-contact or second-attempt wording appears in these cases but is not an established rule.
- A succeeded for four small south refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414) and one small east shipment (REQ-2457), but was rejected for other east invoices, north claims, south shipments/claims, large east invoices, north large shipment (REQ-2430), north small refunds (REQ-2432, REQ-2436), east small refund (REQ-2433), and south small invoices (REQ-2449) and small refunds (REQ-2451, REQ-2452). A is not a universal default.
- B succeeded for east small claim with urgency (REQ-2431), north small claims (REQ-2435, REQ-2448), large east invoice with urgency (REQ-2438), and large east claims (REQ-2440, REQ-2446). It was rejected for large north refund (REQ-2400), large south claim (REQ-2434), north small refund (REQ-2436), north small shipments (REQ-2437, REQ-2445), south small claim/shipment (REQ-2441, REQ-2459), large east refund (REQ-2443), north small invoice (REQ-2444), small east invoice/refund (REQ-2454, REQ-2455), and large east invoice without demonstrated urgency (REQ-2447).
- Best guidance: use A only where directly supported, especially the tested small east shipment; B has positive evidence for north small claims, east claims, and urgent large east invoices; C is supported for tested large south claims/refunds.
- No reliable general rule exists for most region/type/size combinations. Sender department, urgency, wording, and origin have not independently established routing rules.
